headline: Revenue growth and cost cuts flip operations to profit
summary_short: nCino reported FY2026 Q2 revenue of $159.4M, up 10.6% y/y, with gross profit of $100.9M (+16.8% y/y) and operations swinging to a $21.1M profit from a $1.5M operating loss a year ago; net income attributable to nCino was $13.6M versus $5.6M a year ago.
summary_long: Subscription revenue rose 12.2% y/y to $140.9M (88.4% of revenue): 72.6% from existing-customer expansion, 27.4% from new customers. Gross margin rose to 63.3% from 60.0%. Opex fell after the prior workforce reduction: R&D -$4.5M (headcount -92), G&A -$4.4M, while S&M rose only $0.8M, swinging operating income to +$21.1M from a $1.5M loss a year ago. Net income was $13.6M vs $5.6M, aided by a lower tax rate (10.1% vs 43.0%). Cash was $102.8M; a new $200M term loan partly funded a $100M accelerated buyback ($110.5M repurchased this quarter). RPO was $1.3B.

drivers.explanation: Subscription-led revenue growth combined with lower R&D/G&A headcount costs after the Q2 FY2026 workforce reduction, swinging operations from a loss to a $21.1M profit.
Subscription revenue growth: 72.6% from expansion within existing customers, 27.4% from new customers who didn't contribute a year ago; professional services revenue was flat.
Gross margin rose to 63.3% from 60.0% because revenue grew 10.6% y/y while cost of revenue grew only about 1.4%.
R&D expense fell $4.5M and G&A fell $4.4M on headcount cuts (R&D headcount -92) from the prior workforce reduction, while S&M rose only $0.8M on higher commissions.
Also aided by a lower effective tax rate, 10.1% versus 43.0% a year ago, attributed to changes in valuation allowance and profitability.
Tracks the net income increase against a roughly stable weighted diluted share count.
